mainTopic: Danger as a time of heavenly judgment: childbirth, perilous crossings, illness and its advocates, and the sins for which women die
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a דרשה: neglecting חלה and the שבת נר puts a woman's נשמה at risk. The גמרא asks why this judgment comes specifically at childbirth. Five אמוראים answer with folk sayings that all mean one thing: a moment of danger is a moment of judgment. For men, ריש לקיש says the equivalent is crossing a bridge or anything like it. Stories follow about רב, שמואל, רבי ינאי and רבי זירא avoiding danger, and רבי ינאי teaches never to rely on a נס, because even a נס is deducted from one's זכויות. The גמרא then pictures illness as a heavenly trial. A sick person must bring זכות, a dying person says וידוי, and his defense attorneys are תשובה and מעשים טובים, so even one part of merit in a thousand can save him. Next come ברייתות on the sins for which women die in childbirth or young, and on עמי הארץ who call the ארון הקודש 'ארנא'. The עמוד ends as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל begins to teach that הקדש, תרומות and מעשרות are the very body of the תורה, a statement that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: God's warning about חלה and the שבת lamp
steps.stepSummary: The end of a דרשה: God called ישראל 'ראשית' and commanded the 'ראשית' of dough (חלה). He called the נשמה a 'נר' and commanded the שבת נר. If these are kept, good; if not, He takes the נשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I called you 'first,' so I warned you about matters of 'first' (חלה). The soul I placed in you is called a 'lamp,' so I warned you about matters of the lamp (the שבת נר). If you keep them, good. If not, I will take your soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a דרשה, begun on the previous עמוד, explaining why the משנה's sins of חלה and נר are punished with death in childbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each punishment matches its מצוה. ישראל is called 'ראשית', and חלה is taken from the 'ראשית' of the dough. The נשמה is called a 'נר', and the מצוה is the שבת נר. Neglecting a מצוה connected to the נשמה puts the נשמה itself at risk.

keyTerms.meaning: First; refers both to ישראל (ירמיה ב:ג) and to the first of the dough, חלה (במדבר טו:כ)
Lamp; here both the soul (משלי כ:כז) and the Shabbat lamp

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a longer דרשה that started on the previous עמוד (the earlier part covered נדה and דם). Read it as a continuation.

phrases.english: I called you 'first' —
phrases.notes: ירמיה ב:ג: 'קדש ישראל לה' ראשית תבואתה'

phrases.english: so I warned you about matters of 'first.'
The soul that I placed in you is called a 'lamp' —
so I warned you about matters of the lamp.
If you fulfill them — good,
and if not — I will take your soul.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵאשִׁית קָרָאתִי אֶתְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the דרשה earlier on the משנה's three sins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglect of חלה and the שבת נר puts the נשמה at risk, measure for measure.

steps.title: Why specifically at the time of childbirth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if these sins are punished, why does the punishment come specifically during childbirth?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about the time they give birth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next five answers: why is the moment of birth the time of judgment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרשה explained why these sins bring death, but not why the death comes at birth. The question is about timing. Several אמוראים will answer that a moment of danger opens a person up to judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this case specifically?

phrases.english: And what is different about the time of their childbirth?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא בִּשְׁעַת לֵידָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the timing of the punishment just described
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why judgment for these sins takes effect specifically during childbirth

steps.title: רבא: When the ox falls, sharpen the knife
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a proverb: once the ox has fallen, that is the moment to sharpen the knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The ox fell — sharpen the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first answer, a folk saying: when someone is already weak and in danger, that is when judgment strikes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the ox stands, it is hard to slaughter. Once it falls, it is easy, so you grab the knife. A woman giving birth is already 'fallen', in a weak and dangerous state, so her sins are collected then.

phrases.english: Rava said: The ox has fallen —
sharpen the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא נְפַל תּוֹרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of timing
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A moment of weakness and danger is the moment when judgment is carried out.

steps.title: אביי: The insolent maidservant gets one blow for everything
steps.stepSummary: אביי says: when a maidservant's insolence piles up, she is punished for all of it with one blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When the maidservant's insolence increases, it will all be paid with one stick.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second proverb explaining why judgment comes at childbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master holds back while the servant keeps misbehaving, then punishes everything at once. Childbirth is already painful because of חוה's sin, and at that moment the woman's own sins are added to that one 'blow'.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When the maidservant's insolence abounds,
it will be with a single blow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר תַּפִּישׁ תֵּירוּס אַמְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel proverb answering the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Accumulated sins are punished together at one painful moment.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Leave the drunk, he falls by himself
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says: leave the drunkard alone and he will fall on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Leave the drunk, for he falls by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a third proverb with a slightly different idea: no active punishment is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Childbirth is dangerous by nature. If הקב"ה simply withholds special protection because of her sins, the danger itself can cause harm. Nobody needs to push the drunk.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Leave the drunkard,
for he falls on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר שִׁבְקֵיהּ לְרַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another proverb for the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The natural danger of childbirth is enough when divine protection is withdrawn.

steps.title: מר עוקבא: The lame shepherd settles accounts at the pen
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא says: a lame shepherd cannot catch running goats, but at the gate of the pen he scolds and inside he settles the account.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said: The shepherd is lame and the goats are running. At the gate of the pen, words; at the pen itself, the reckoning.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא gives a fourth proverb: judgment waits for the right moment, when the person is 'cornered'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While a woman is healthy, her sins are left pending, like goats running free. At childbirth she enters a narrow, dangerous place, like the pen. There her account is reviewed to decide whether she deserves a נס.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva said:
The shepherd is lame and the goats are running,
at the gate, words,
and in the pen, the reckoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר רָעֲיָא חֲגִרָא וְעִיזֵּי רָהֲטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another proverb for the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sins are held in abeyance until a moment of danger, when the full account is reviewed.

steps.title: רב פפא: Friends at the shop, none at the gate of disgrace
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says: when business is good, a person has many friends; in disgrace, he has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: At the entrance to the shops, brothers and friends are many. At the gate of disgrace, there are no brothers and no friends.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the fifth and last proverb: in hard times, a person's protections disappear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In good times a person has many 'friends' who stand by him. In a time of danger like childbirth, the heavenly voices that might have spoken up for her fall away. She is left on her own, and her record is judged.
steps.whatToRemember: All five proverbs teach one idea: a moment of danger is a moment of judgment. That is why the three sins of the משנה are punished specifically at childbirth.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
At the entrance to the shops, brothers and friends abound,

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּב בִּזְיוֹנֵי — לָא אַחֵי וְלָא מְרַחֲמֵי.
phrases.english: at the gate of disgrace — no brothers and no friends.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר אַבָּב חַנְוָאתָא נְפִישִׁי אַחֵי וּמְרַחֲמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final proverb in the series
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In times of trouble a person loses supporters, so only true merit saves him.

steps.title: When are men examined?
steps.stepSummary: If women are judged at childbirth, the גמרא asks when men are judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And men, where are they examined?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that sets up ריש לקיש's answer: what is the male version of childbirth?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that 'danger brings judgment' should apply to men too. Men do not give birth, so the גמרא looks for their equivalent dangerous moment.

phrases.english: And men — where are they examined?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגַבְרֵי הֵיכָא מִיבַּדְקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle just established to men
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The male equivalent of the dangerous moment of childbirth

steps.title: ריש לקיש: When crossing a bridge
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that men are judged when they cross a bridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: At the time when they cross over a bridge.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question: crossing a bridge is the dangerous moment for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old bridges were often unsafe, so crossing one was a real danger. At that moment a man's merits are reviewed, just like a woman's at childbirth.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
At the time when they cross over a bridge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעוֹבְרִים עַל הַגֶּשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Men are judged when crossing a bridge.

steps.title: Only a bridge and nothing else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: is a bridge really the only dangerous place?
steps.simpleTranslation: A bridge, and nothing more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on how narrow ריש לקיש's answer sounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, the answer suggests that bridges are the only moment of danger for men. That seems too limited, since men face many dangers.

phrases.english: A bridge and nothing else?

steps.triggerLanguage: גֶּשֶׁר וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrow wording of ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'bridge' in ריש לקיש's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limiting judgment to bridges alone is unreasonably narrow.

steps.title: Read it as: anything like a bridge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: read ריש לקיש as 'anything like a bridge', meaning any dangerous place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: something like a bridge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by widening the meaning of ריש לקיש's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bridge was only an example. Any place of real danger counts as a moment of judgment for men.

phrases.english: Say: something like a bridge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא כְּעֵין גֶּשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: Any comparable place of danger brings judgment
steps.whatToRemember: Men are judged in any situation of danger. A bridge is just the example.

steps.title: רב avoided a ferry with a gentile on board
steps.stepSummary: רב would not cross on a ferry that had a גוי aboard, fearing he would be caught up in the גוי's judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would not cross on a ferry in which a גוי sat. He said: Perhaps judgment will be decreed on him, and I will be caught along with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing how רב acted on the idea that danger brings judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A river crossing is 'like a bridge', a time of judgment. רב feared that if another passenger was being punished, the boat might sink and take him down too. He avoided adding risk.

phrases.english: Rav would not cross on a ferry
in which a gentile was sitting,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: דִילְמָא מִיפְּקִיד לֵיהּ דִּינָא עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: he said: Perhaps judgment will be reckoned against him
and I will be caught together with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב לָא עָבַר בְּמַבָּרָא דְּיָתֵיב בֵּיהּ גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the principle that a 'bridge-like' danger brings judgment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a dangerous crossing, avoid company that may bring judgment on the whole boat.

steps.title: שמואל preferred a ferry with a gentile on board
steps.stepSummary: שמואל took the opposite approach: he crossed only on a ferry with a גוי aboard, because the שטן does not rule over two nations at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would only cross on a ferry that had a גוי in it. He said: The שטן does not have power over two nations at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite practice of שמואל, with his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that crossing is a time of judgment. They disagree on how a mixed group affects it. רב feared being swept up with someone else, while שמואל held that judgment is not carried out on two nations together, so a mixed boat is safer.
steps.confusionAlert: רב and שמואל do not disagree about whether crossing water is dangerous. Both agree it is. They only disagree about whether a mixed group adds or reduces the risk.

phrases.english: Shmuel would cross only on a ferry
that had a gentile in it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: שִׂטְנָא בִּתְרֵי אוּמֵּי לָא שָׁלֵיט.
phrases.english: he said: Satan does not have power over two nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל לָא עָבַר אֶלָּא בְּמַבָּרָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposite practice to רב's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixed group of two nations is protected, because judgment does not strike two nations together.

steps.title: רבי ינאי inspected before crossing
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי would check the bridge or ferry first and only then cross.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי would inspect and then cross.
steps.whatsHappening: A third practice: רבי ינאי examined the crossing for safety before using it. The next step explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of focusing on who else is aboard, רבי ינאי took practical steps to lower the actual danger. This sets up the גמרא's explanation of his reasoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai would inspect and then cross.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי בָּדֵיק וְעָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another sage's behavior at a dangerous crossing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Check a dangerous crossing before using it.

steps.title: רבי ינאי's rule: never rely on a נס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי ינאי acted on his own principle: do not stand in danger expecting a נס, because it may not happen, and if it does, it is deducted from your זכויות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי follows his own view, for he said: A person should never stand in a place of danger and say that a miracle will be done for him, because perhaps no miracle will be done. And if a miracle is done for him, it is deducted from his merits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links רבי ינאי's careful behavior to a principle he stated elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reasons to avoid danger. First, the נס might not come. Second, even if it comes, it 'costs' you, because your זכויות are used up to pay for it. So the wise path is to avoid needing a נס at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous practical principle: a person may not rely on miracles, and must take normal precautions against danger.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai follows his reasoning, for he said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בְּמָקוֹם סַכָּנָה
phrases.english: A person should never stand in a place of danger
saying that a miracle will be performed for him,
lest no miracle be performed for him.
And if a miracle is performed for him —
it is deducted from his merits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי ינאי's practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not rely on a נס in danger. It may not come, and if it does, it reduces one's זכויות.

steps.title: רבי חנין's verse: יעקב's merits were diminished
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין brings a פסוק as the source: יעקב said 'קטנתי מכל החסדים', meaning his merits shrank because of the kindnesses done for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said: What is the verse for this? 'I have become small from all the kindnesses and all the truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנין gives a פסוק that supports רבי ינאי's idea that a נס is deducted from one's merits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב says 'קטנתי', 'I have become small', because of all the חסדים God did for him. The kindness he received used up his זכויות, which is exactly רבי ינאי's point.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said: What is the verse?
'I am diminished by all the kindnesses and by all the truth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנִין מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a scriptural source for רבי ינאי's rule
steps.raayaObject: That a נס or divine kindness is deducted from one's merits
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית לב:יא, יעקב's words 'קטנתי מכל החסדים'

steps.title: רבי זירא avoided palm trees on a windy day
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא would not walk among palm trees on a day of strong southern wind, in case a tree fell on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא, on a day of southern wind, would not go out among the palm trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this section with another story of a sage who avoided a place of danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strong winds could knock down palm trees. רבי זירא did not rely on a נס and kept away, putting רבי ינאי's principle into practice in everyday life.
steps.whatToRemember: Danger brings judgment, for women at childbirth and for men in any 'bridge-like' situation. Therefore one must avoid danger and never rely on a נס, as רבי ינאי, רב, שמואל and רבי זירא each showed in practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira, on a day of southern wind,
would not go out among the palm trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא בְּיוֹמָא דְשׁוּתָא לָא נָפֵיק לְבֵינֵי דִּיקְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example of avoiding danger in line with רבי ינאי's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid even ordinary natural dangers rather than relying on divine protection.

steps.title: Pray not to fall ill, because a sick person must prove his merit
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה teaches that a person should always pray not to get sick, because once sick, he is told to bring merit in order to be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, the son of רב יהודה, said: A person should always ask for mercy that he not become sick. If he becomes sick, they say to him: Bring proof of merit, and be released.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה that fits the theme of the earlier steps: avoid situations where you are put on trial in Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being healthy means you are not being judged right now. Once you are sick, the case is opened, and you need enough זכות to get out of it. That is why it is better to pray in advance that it never comes to that.

keyTerms.meaning: Merit; a point in one's favor

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the frame for everything that follows: illness is pictured as a court case, and merit is the way out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda said:
A person should always ask for mercy
that he not become sick,
for if he becomes sick, they say to him:
Bring merit and be released.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: לְעוֹלָם יְבַקֵּשׁ אָדָם רַחֲמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of avoiding danger (steps 12-17), now applied to illness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pray not to get sick, because a sick person must show merit to be saved.

steps.title: מר עוקבא's verse: the one who falls must bring the proof
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא finds the source in the פסוק 'כי יפול הנופל ממנו' and reads 'ממנו' as 'from him': the proof must come from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said: What is the verse for this? 'If the faller falls from it (ממנו)'. Read ממנו as 'from him': from him the proof must be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא gives a פסוק as the source for רב יצחק's idea that a sick person has to prove his own merit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about a person falling off a roof without a railing. מר עוקבא reads the word ממנו ('from it') as 'from him'. So the person who 'falls' into trouble is the one who has to bring the proof that he deserves to be saved.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If the faller falls from it' (דברים כב:ח)

steps.confusionAlert: In its plain meaning, ממנו means 'from the roof'. מר עוקבא is reading it in a new way as 'from him (the faller)'. Do not mix up the plain meaning with the דרשה.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva said: What is the verse? —
'If the faller falls from it' —
phrases.notes: דברים כב:ח, about building a railing on a roof

phrases.english: 'from him' — to bring proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב יצחק's statement that a sick person must bring merit to be released
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים כב:ח, 'כי יפול הנופל ממנו', read as 'from him the proof must come'

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: the faller was destined to fall, but guilt comes through the guilty
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the same פסוק differently: the man was destined to fall since creation, which is why he is already called 'the faller'. Still, it happens through the owner who is guilty, because merit is brought about through the meritorious and guilt through the guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'If the faller falls from it' — this person was set to fall from the six days of creation, because he has not fallen yet and the verse already calls him 'the faller'. But merit is brought about through a worthy person and guilt through a guilty person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another way to read the same פסוק, this time from the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why the פסוק calls him 'the faller' before he has fallen. The answer is that his fall was decided long ago. Even so, the homeowner is still blamed, because Heaven arranges for bad things to happen through people who are already guilty (here, the one who did not build a railing).

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
They bring about; they 'roll' events toward
A meritorious person / a guilty person

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'מגלגלין זכות על ידי זכאי וחובה על ידי חייב' is a well-known idea: Heaven chooses who will be the means for good or bad outcomes.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'If the faller falls from it' —

phrases.aramaic: רָאוּי זֶה לִיפּוֹל מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית,
phrases.english: this one was fit to fall from the six days of creation,
for he has not yet fallen, yet the verse calls him 'the faller'.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, שֶׁמְגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת עַל יְדֵי זַכַּאי
phrases.english: Rather, merit is brought about through a worthy person
and guilt through a guilty person.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כִּי יִפּוֹל הַנּוֹפֵל מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק that מר עוקבא used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The faller was destined to fall, but the harm is brought about through the guilty homeowner.

steps.title: A dangerously ill person is told to confess
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who is sick and close to death is told to do וידוי, since all who are executed by בית דין confess.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who became sick and is close to death, they say to him: Confess, for all those who are executed confess.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about what to tell a person who is very sick: he should say וידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone executed by בית דין confesses so that his death will be a כפרה. A very sick person is compared to him, so he too should confess. This continues the picture of illness as a kind of judgment.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי שֶׁחָלָה וְנָטָה לָמוּת,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who became sick and is close to death,
they say to him: Confess,
for all those who are executed confess.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי שֶׁחָלָה וְנָטָה לָמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that a sick person is under judgment (step 18).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who is close to death should say וידוי, like one being executed.

steps.title: Stages of danger compared to arrest, chains, and trial
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: going to the market is like being handed to a soldier, a headache is like being put in a neck chain, and falling sick in bed is like being brought up for trial. Only one with great defense attorneys is saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a person goes out to the market, he should see himself as someone handed over to a soldier. If his head hurts, he should see himself as someone put in a chain. If he went to bed sick, he should see himself as someone brought up to the platform to be judged. Anyone brought up to be judged is saved if he has great defense attorneys, and if not, he is not saved.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists three rising levels of danger and compares each one to a step in being arrested and tried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage is more serious: first under guard, then chained, then on trial. The last image leads into the key point: at trial, what saves you is good defense attorneys. This sets up the next line, which tells us who those attorneys are.

keyTerms.meaning: A soldier / officer who guards prisoners
A chain or collar around a prisoner's neck

phrases.english: When a person goes out to the market,

phrases.aramaic: יְהִי דּוֹמֶה בְּעֵינָיו כְּמִי שֶׁנִּמְסַר לְסַרְדְּיוֹט.
phrases.english: he should see himself as one handed over to a soldier.
If his head hurts —

phrases.aramaic: יְהִי דּוֹמֶה בְּעֵינָיו כְּמִי שֶׁנְּתָנוּהוּ בְּקוֹלָר.
phrases.english: he should see himself as one placed in a neck chain.
If he went up to bed and fell ill —

phrases.aramaic: יְהִי דּוֹמֶה בְּעֵינָיו כְּמִי שֶׁהֶעְלוּהוּ לַגַּרְדּוֹם לִידּוֹן,
phrases.english: he should see himself as one brought up to the platform to be judged,
for anyone brought up to the platform to be judged —

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ פְּרַקְלִיטִין גְּדוֹלִים — נִיצּוֹל,
phrases.english: if he has great defense attorneys, he is saved,
and if not, he is not saved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם יוֹצֵא לַשּׁוּק, יְהִי דּוֹמֶה בְּעֵינָיו כְּמִי שֶׁנִּמְסַר לְסַרְדְּיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, expanding the comparison of danger to judgment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each level of danger is like a stage of trial, and only great defense attorneys save a person.

steps.title: A person's defense attorneys are repentance and good deeds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא names the 'defense attorneys' in Heavenly judgment: תשובה and מעשים טובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are a person's defense attorneys: repentance and good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא explains the image from the last step: in Heaven's court, your defense attorneys are תשובה and מעשים טובים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said you need great attorneys to be saved. This step tells you what they are in real life. This is the practical lesson: a person builds his defense through תשובה and good deeds.
steps.whatToRemember: In Heaven's court, a person's defense attorneys are תשובה and מעשים טובים.

phrases.english: And these are a person's defense attorneys:
repentance and good deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן פְּרַקְלִיטִין שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'פרקליטין' mentioned in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה and מעשים טובים are a person's advocates.

steps.title: Even one advocate against 999 accusers saves him
steps.stepSummary: Even if 999 accuse a person and only one speaks for him, he is saved, as the פסוק in איוב says 'one advocate among a thousand'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if 999 argue that he is guilty and one argues that he has merit, he is saved, as it says: 'If there is for him an angel, an advocate, one among a thousand, to tell of a man's uprightness, then He is gracious to him and says: Save him from going down to the pit, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that even very little defense is enough, and proves it from a פסוק in איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that one voice of merit outweighs 999 voices of guilt. The פסוק speaks of 'one advocate among a thousand', and still ה' says to save him. So even a small amount of merit can rescue a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Argue against him; speak of his guilt
From going down to the pit (death)

phrases.english: And even if nine hundred ninety-nine
argue for his guilt
and one argues for his merit — he is saved,
as it says: 'If there is for him an angel, an advocate,
one among a thousand,
to tell of a man's uprightness,
then He is gracious to him and says:
Save him from going down to the pit, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת וְתִשְׁעִים וְתִשְׁעָה מְלַמְּדִים עָלָיו חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that even a tiny defense works, with a proof from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That one advocate against 999 accusers is enough to save a person
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב לג:כג-כד, 'מלאך מליץ אחד מני אלף... פדעהו מרדת שחת'

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי: even one part in a thousand within the same angel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי goes further: even if 999 parts of that same single angel's report are against him and only one part is for him, he is saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר, son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, says: Even if 999 parts of that same angel are for guilt and one is for merit, he is saved, as it says: 'An advocate, one among a thousand.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second view reads the same פסוק in an even stronger way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view spoke of 999 separate accusers and one separate advocate. רבי אליעזר says the 'one in a thousand' is inside one angel's own report: even if that single advocate finds only one part in a thousand of merit, it is enough. This makes the power of a small merit even greater.

keyTerms.meaning: Within that same angel (in his own report)

steps.whatToRemember: Even the smallest piece of merit can save a person from a harsh judgment.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
Even if nine hundred ninety-nine
parts within that same angel are for guilt
and one is for merit — he is saved,
as it says: 'An advocate, one among a thousand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stronger reading of the same פסוק from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one part merit out of a thousand within a single angel's report saves a person.

steps.title: Three sins for which women die in childbirth, and רבי אלעזר's version
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: for three sins women die in childbirth (יולדות). רבי אלעזר reads it as women die young (ילדות).
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: For three sins women die in childbirth. רבי אלעזר says: women die young.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא connected to the משנה's three sins: נדה, חלה, and הדלקת הנר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says these three sins cause women to die in childbirth (יולדות). רבי אלעזר has a different version: they die young (ילדות). The two readings differ in only one letter, but they describe different punishments.

keyTerms.meaning: Three sins (נדה, חלה, הדלקת הנר, from the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: יולדות and ילדות look almost the same. יולדות means 'giving birth'; ילדות means 'young'. That one-letter difference is the whole disagreement.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: For three sins
women die in childbirth.
Rabbi Elazar says:
women die young.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת נָשִׁים מֵתוֹת יוֹלְדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's theme of the three sins after the long side discussion on danger and judgment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For three sins women die in childbirth (or, per רבי אלעזר, die young).

steps.title: רבי אחא: for washing children's soiled clothes on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא gives a different sin: women die for washing their children's dirty clothes on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא says: For the sin of washing their children's dirt on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא offers another sin that brings this punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of only the three sins from the משנה, רבי אחא names a specific חילול שבת: washing out children's soiled clothing on שבת, which is the מלאכה of laundering.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha says:
for the sin of washing their children's excrement on Shabbos.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר בְּעָוֹן שֶׁמְּכַבְּסוֹת צוֹאַת בְּנֵיהֶם בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different cause for the punishment in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are punished for laundering children's soiled clothes on שבת.

steps.title: יש אומרים: for calling the Holy Ark just 'ארנא'
steps.stepSummary: Others say the punishment is for calling the ארון הקודש by the plain name 'ארנא' (box), without respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: Because they call the Holy Ark 'arna' (a box).
steps.whatsHappening: A final opinion gives yet another cause: disrespectful speech about the ארון הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the holy ark a plain 'box' shows a lack of respect for something holy. According to this view, that lack of respect is serious enough to bring the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy Ark holding the ספר תורה

phrases.english: And some say:
because they call the Holy Ark 'a box'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: עַל שֶׁקּוֹרִין לַאֲרוֹן הַקּוֹדֶשׁ אֲרָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative cause for the punishment in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calling the ארון הקודש a plain 'box' brings this punishment.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the 'ארנא' opinion and adds 'בית עם'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן אלעזר teaches in a ברייתא that עמי הארץ die because of two disrespectful habits. They call the ארון הקודש 'ארנא' (box), and they call the בית הכנסת 'בית עם' (people's house).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל בן אלעזר says: Because of two sins, ignorant people die. They call the holy Ark 'a box,' and they call the synagogue 'the people's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the 'others say' opinion from the last step. Calling the ארון הקודש 'ארנא' really is treated as a serious sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said that calling the ארון 'ארנא' brings punishment. This ברייתא confirms it with a second source and adds a second, similar sin: calling the בית הכנסת 'בית עם.' Both sins share one idea. They use plain, everyday names for holy things, and that strips away their holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Ignorant, unlearned people who are careless with מצוות
The holy Ark where the ספר תורה is kept
'A box' — a plain, disrespectful name for the Ark
'The people's house' — a plain, disrespectful name for the בית הכנסת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז"ל treat the way we talk about holy places. Even a name can be a form of disrespect.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yishmael ben Elazar says:
Because of the sin of two things
ignorant people die (young)
because they call the holy Ark 'a box,'
and because they call the synagogue 'the people's house.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'others say' opinion of Step 28 with a ברייתא and adds a parallel sin.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that calling the ארון הקודש 'ארנא' brings death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל בן אלעזר.

steps.title: Three danger-points for a woman: נדה, חלה and הדלקת הנר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that three things are 'death danger-points' for a woman. They are נדה, חלה and הדלקת הנר. His teaching comes in two versions: בדקי מיתה (places of being checked) or דבקי מיתה (things that bring death closer).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says: Three 'checkpoints of death' were created in a woman. Some say it as: three 'clingers of death.' They are: the laws of נדה, separating חלה, and lighting the שבת candles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, from רבי יוסי. It names three specific מצוות that put a woman in danger if she is careless with them. The text of his statement has two versions, with just one letter switched (ב or ד).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to the משנה's three sins for which women die. 'בדקי' means places where a person is examined, meaning her record is checked when she is in danger. 'דבקי' means things that stick to a person and bring death closer. The next step will explain why there are two versions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Checkpoints of death' — times when a person's deeds are examined, during danger
'Things that cling with death' — sins that bring death closer

steps.confusionAlert: בדקי and דבקי look almost the same. Only the ב and ד switch places. Do not read them as two different lists. It is the same three מצוות, described with two different words.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei says:
Three checkpoints of death were created in a woman,
and some say: three things that cling with death:
menstrual purity, challah, and lighting the candle.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of women's three sins and brings רבי יוסי's ברייתא with two versions of its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נדה, חלה and הדלקת הנר are the three מצוות that endanger a woman if she is careless with them.

steps.title: Each version matches a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two versions. One version follows רבי אלעזר, who says women die young. The other follows the רבנן, who say women die in childbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: One version is according to רבי אלעזר, and the other version is according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוסי's ברייתא has two versions. Each version fits one side of the argument from Step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 26 the רבנן read the text as 'women die in childbirth' (יולדות). רבי אלעזר read it as 'women die young' (ילדות). 'בדקי מיתה' means being checked at a moment of danger, which fits the רבנן and childbirth. 'דבקי מיתה' means sins that bring death closer at any time, which fits רבי אלעזר and dying young.
steps.whatToRemember: בדקי = the רבנן (danger during childbirth, when she is 'checked'). דבקי = רבי אלעזר (sins that bring death closer, so she dies young).

phrases.english: One (version) is like Rabbi Elazar,
and one is like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וַחֲדָא כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two versions of the wording in Step 30 by tying them to the argument in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each textual version to a different תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the two versions are just a random copying difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each wording follows its own opinion: דבקי follows רבי אלעזר (dying young), and בדקי follows the רבנן (dying in childbirth).

steps.title: The laws of הקדש, תרומות and מעשרות are the very body of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches in a ברייתא that the laws of הקדש, תרומות and מעשרות are the essential 'body' of the תורה. His statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: The laws of holy property, תרומות and מעשרות are themselves the main body of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that stresses how serious these laws are. This is only the start of the statement, which continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה was just mentioned, and it is a kind of תרומה. So the גמרא now brings a teaching that these laws are central and very severe, not minor details. 'הן הן' means 'these themselves are,' which emphasizes that these laws are the core of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
Portions of produce given to the כהן
Tithes, the tenth portions of produce
The main body, or essence, of the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. It ends with a comma and continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
The laws of consecrated property, terumot, and tithes —
they themselves are the essence of Torah,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After mentioning חלה (a form of תרומה), the גמרא brings a ברייתא on how serious the laws of הקדש, תרומות and מעשרות are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of הקדש, תרומות and מעשרות are the very essence of the תורה. The statement continues on the next עמוד.
